_about: ADR Decision 613: questions asking what one drug does to her, each with the findings the demo replica injected for it on 2026-11-10 (duplicate-order findings, which production never puts to the model, left out), each labelled related, unrelated or borderline by whether what it states bears on the effect, reaction or reason the question names. Borderline is printed and not scored.

findings.finding: Fluconazole interacts with active order Nevirapine — Moderate. Coadministration with fluconazole may increase the plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of CYP450 3A4. The mechanism is decreased clearance due to inhibition of CYP450 3A4-mediated metabolism by fluconazole, a moderate inhibitor of the isoenzyme.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Tramadol interacts with active order Nevirapine — Moderate. Coadministration with inducers of CYP450 3A4 may decrease the plasma concentrations of tramadol, which is primarily metabolized by CYP450 3A4 and 2D6.  Reduced opioid efficacy can occur, including opioid withdrawal in physically dependent patients.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Erythromycin interacts with active order Nevirapine — Moderate. Coadministration with nevirapine may decrease the plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy of drugs that are substrates of CYP450 3A4. The proposed mechanism is increased clearance due to nevirapine-mediated induction of CYP450 3A4.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Trimethoprim interacts with active order Lamivudine — Minor. In a study with 14 HIV-positive patients, coadministration of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole DS once a day for 5 days) and lamivudine (300 mg single dose on day 5) resulted in a mean decrease of 35% in lamivudine renal clearance and a mean increase of 43% in lamivudine area under the plasma concentration-time curve. The mechanism of interaction is thought to be competitive inhibition of tubular secretion by trimethoprim. Lamivudine did not affect the pharmacokinetic profile of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. Given the favorable safety profile of lamivudine, this interaction is unlikely to be of clinical significance. However, patients with renal dysfunction should be monitored carefully and the lamivudine dose adjusted if necessary. In addition, it should be noted that the effect of higher dosages of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole on lamivudine pharmacokinetics has not been investigated.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Isoniazid interacts with active order Stavudine — Moderate. The risk of peripheral neuropathy may be increased during concurrent use of two or more agents that are associated with this adverse effect. Patient risk factors include diabetes and age older than 60 years.
findings.label: related

findings.finding: Efavirenz interacts with active order Nevirapine — Moderate. Coadministration of nevirapine and efavirenz has resulted in increased toxicity without additional therapeutic benefit over either agent alone. The mechanism of interaction has not been established, although this combination has exhibited strong antagonistic anti-HIV-1 activity in cell culture. Efavirenz is in the same ATC class (J05AG) as active order Nevirapine — possible duplicate therapy
findings.label: unrelated

The precise mechanism of interaction has not been established, but may involve rifampin induction of fluconazole metabolism via CYP450 isoenzymes, although fluconazole is not extensively metabolized but is primarily (approximately 80%) eliminated unchanged by the kidney.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Fluconazole interacts with active order Efavirenz — Major. Efavirenz can cause significant QT interval prolongation in patients with the CYP450 2B6 *6/*6 genotype due to reduced metabolic clearance of the drug stemming from decreased levels of functional CYP450 2B6 isoenzyme.
findings.label: unrelated

findings.finding: Fluconazole interacts with active order Sulfamethoxazole — Minor. Limited data suggest that sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (SMX-TMP) may rarely prolong the QT interval of the electrocardiogram. Theoretically, coadministration with other agents that can prolong the QT interval may result in additive effects and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias including torsade de pointes and sudden death. There have been isolated reports of QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias occurring in patients treated with SMX-TMP intravenously. Patients should be advised to seek prompt medical attention if they experience symptoms that could indicate the occurrence of torsade de pointes such as dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, palpitation, irregular heart rhythm, shortness of breath, or syncope.
findings.label: unrelated

The coadministration of clarithromycin and rifabutin at normally recommended dosages has been reported to have resulted in significantly altered pharmacokinetics for both drugs. Other macrolide antibiotics may interact in a similar manner with rifamycins.

findings.finding: Sulfamethoxazole interacts with active order Lamivudine / zidovudine — Minor. Limited data indicate that zidovudine may significantly increase the serum half-life of both trimethoprim (TMP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX). The mechanism is not known, but may be related to an increase in the volume of distribution of each drug. However, net clearance is not affected because zidovudine is mostly metabolized and the glucuronide may be eliminated via biliary excretion. This interaction is not likely to be clinically important except when hepatic glucuronidation is also impaired by liver disease or drug inhibition.

findings.finding: Sulfamethoxazole interacts with active order Zidovudine — Minor. Limited data indicate that zidovudine may significantly increase the serum half-life of both trimethoprim (TMP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX). The mechanism is not known, but may be related to an increase in the volume of distribution of each drug. In addition, trimethoprim can decrease the renal clearance of zidovudine and its glucuronide metabolite by inhibiting their tubular secretion. findings.finding: Trimethoprim interacts with active order Lamivudine — Minor.
